auth login:
Usage: kagura-memory auth login [OPTIONS]

  Authenticate via OAuth2 device flow.

  Examples:
    kagura-memory auth login                      # read + write (default)
    kagura-memory auth login --read-only          # read-only
    kagura-memory auth login --scope "memory:read memory:write profile:read"  # custom
    kagura-memory auth login --profile work
    kagura-memory auth login --no-browser         # for SSH / headless
    kagura-memory auth login --invite https://<host>/join/<token>  # invite-only sign-up

  --invite signs a new account up with a beta invite and approves this login
  from one link, on a server that supports it. An older server gets two steps
  instead, and one that takes no invites a notice. The invite is never saved,
  and is printed only inside a link.

Options:
  --profile TEXT          Profile name to store credentials under (default:
                          'default').
  --server URL            MCP server URL to authenticate against
  --scope TEXT            OAuth scope (default: 'memory:read memory:write').
                          Override only if you need a custom scope set.
  --read-only             Request read-only scope ('memory:read') instead of the
                          default read+write.
  --no-browser            Don't try to open a browser — just print the URL and
                          code.
  --invite LINK_OR_TOKEN  Sign up with an invite: the
                          https://<host>/join/<token> link you were sent, or its
                          bare token. Checked locally; never stored.
  --help                  Show this message and exit.

Usage: kagura-memory auth logout [OPTIONS]

  Revoke server-side and delete the local profile (or all of them).

  The server-side revoke is best effort: the profile is deleted even when it
  fails. Asks first unless --yes; with nothing stored, a logout that names no
  profile succeeds. --all does not take --profile.

Options:
  --profile TEXT  Profile to log out (default: default profile).
  --all           Delete every profile and remove the credentials file.
  -y, --yes       Skip the confirmation prompt.
  --help          Show this message and exit.
auth refresh:
Usage: kagura-memory auth refresh [OPTIONS]

  Rotate access_token (optionally requesting a new scope).

  Examples:
    kagura-memory auth refresh
    kagura-memory auth refresh --scope "memory:read"                       # narrow to read-only
    kagura-memory auth refresh --scope "memory:read memory:write"          # widen (triggers device flow)
    kagura-memory auth refresh --profile work

  A refresh token works once (memory-cloud v0.79.0+). The refresh is shared with
  kagura-memory-mcp and every client: all of them refresh under one lock on
  credentials.json and re-read it first, so when one of them rotated the token
  meanwhile, this command keeps that token instead of sending the used refresh
  token again, and says so. With --scope it always asks the server, using the
  refresh token on file at that moment. A password reset revokes every OAuth
  token of the account (v0.83.0+), so a refresh after one fails; run `kagura-
  memory auth login`.

Options:
  --profile TEXT  Profile to refresh (default: default profile).
  --scope TEXT    Request this scope (default: keep the current grant
                  unchanged). Pass space-separated values to ask for multiple
                  (e.g. 'memory:read memory:write'). If wider than the current
                  grant, re-runs the device flow.
  --no-browser    Don't try to open a browser — just print the URL and code.
  --help          Show this message and exit.

Usage: kagura-memory context search-config [OPTIONS] CONTEXT_ID

  Update search configuration for a context.

  Weights must sum to 1.0. The weights and reranker settings need context editor
  access; --content-chunks and --llm-selector need the context owner or a
  workspace owner/admin, and where the deployment gates them by plan, the plan's
  feature and a free slot.

  Examples:
    kagura-memory context search-config CTX_UUID --semantic 0.5 --bm25 0.5
    kagura-memory context search-config CTX_UUID --rerank --reranker voyage
    kagura-memory context search-config CTX_UUID --rerank --reranker self_hosted
    kagura-memory context search-config CTX_UUID --content-chunks
    kagura-memory context search-config CTX_UUID --no-llm-selector

Options:
  --semantic FLOAT RANGE          Semantic weight (0.0-1.0)  [0.0<=x<=1.0]
  --bm25 FLOAT RANGE              BM25 weight (0.0-1.0)  [0.0<=x<=1.0]
  --fetch-factor INTEGER RANGE    Fetch multiplier (1-10)  [1<=x<=10]
  --rerank                        Enable reranking
  --no-rerank                     Disable reranking
  --reranker [voyage|cohere|self_hosted]
                                  Reranker provider (self_hosted: the
                                  deployment's keyless local reranker)
  --reranker-model TEXT           Reranker model name
  --content-chunks                Embed long content as chunk vectors; sends
                                  memory content, not only summaries, to the
                                  embedding and rerank providers. Context owner
                                  or workspace owner/admin only (server
                                  v0.110.0+)
  --no-content-chunks             Turn content chunk vectors off (deletes the
                                  chunks)
  --llm-selector                  Let recall send summaries and content to the
                                  deployment's judge model to keep the results
                                  that answer the query. Context owner or
                                  workspace owner/admin only (server v0.115.0+)
  --no-llm-selector               Turn the recall LLM selector off
  --help                          Show this message and exit.

recall:
Usage: kagura-memory recall [OPTIONS] QUERY

  Search memories directly (without AI analysis).

  Without --rerank/--no-rerank the server follows the context's search config
  (memory-cloud v0.69.0+). --rerank applies only when the context enables
  reranking; --no-rerank always skips it.

  The reply is printed as JSON, with each hit's content (when the server sends
  it) right after its summary. --verbosity, --full and --max-chars are sent only
  when given. A server from v0.82.0 that predates one of them refuses it
  (invalid_argument); the command then retries once without the ones the server
  lists as refused (all three it sent when the reply does not list them) and
  says so on stderr.

  Examples:
    kagura-memory recall "FastAPI dependency injection"
    kagura-memory recall "OAuth2 implementation" -k 10
    kagura-memory recall -c dev "error handling pattern"
    kagura-memory recall "latency-sensitive lookup" --no-rerank
    kagura-memory recall "project context" --trusted-only --verbosity full
    kagura-memory recall "deploy runbook" --full 1 --max-chars 40000
    kagura-memory recall "release notes" --full 0

Options:
  -c, --context-id TEXT       Context ID (or set in .kagura.json)
  -k INTEGER                  Number of results  [default: 5]
  --rerank                    Request reranking for this call (default: follow
                              the context's search config)
  --no-rerank                 Skip reranking for this call
  --trusted-only              Exclude external / connector-ingested memories
                              (filters.trust_tier=trusted; server v0.24.0+). Use
                              it for reads fed back to an agent, like the
                              SessionStart hook.
  --verbosity [compact|full]  Result detail (server v0.108.0+). compact, the
                              server default: 160-character summaries without
                              tags; full: uncut summaries, tags, context_summary
                              and scope.
  --full INTEGER RANGE        How many top results carry content, up to 1,500
                              characters each (server v0.114.0+; default: the
                              server's, 3 unless set; 0: summaries only).
                              [0<=x<=100]
  --max-chars INTEGER RANGE   Response budget in characters, 10000-100000
                              (server v0.82.0+; default 20000).
                              [10000<=x<=100000]
  --help                      Show this message and exit.
remember:
Usage: kagura-memory remember [OPTIONS]

  Store a memory directly (without AI analysis).

  Coordinates in --details must be JSON numbers, not strings: the server rejects
  string-typed lat/lon with a 422 by design. Updating a memory replaces details
  wholesale; `kagura-memory update-memory --merge-details` revises location
  while keeping the other keys (or re-send them yourself).

  Examples:
    kagura-memory remember -s "FastAPI DI pattern" --content "Use Depends()..."
    kagura-memory remember -c dev -s "OAuth2 setup" --content "..." --tags "auth,oauth"
    kagura-memory remember -s "Spec" --content "$(cat spec.md)" \
      --source-uri file:///spec.md --source-type file
    kagura-memory remember -s "Coffee with Sato" --content "..." \
      --location "35.68,139.76,Tokyo HQ"
    kagura-memory remember -s "Release 2.0 shipped" --content "..." --observed-at 2026-11-01
    kagura-memory remember -s "Deploy key rotated" --content "..." --dedupe check

Options:
  -c, --context-id TEXT           Context ID (or set in .kagura.json)
  -s, --summary TEXT              Memory summary (for search)  [required]
  --content TEXT                  Memory content (full text)  [required]
  -t, --type TEXT                 Memory type  [default: note]
  -i, --importance FLOAT          Importance 0.0-1.0  [default: 0.5]
  --tags TEXT                     Comma-separated tags (e.g., 'python,fastapi')
  --source-uri TEXT               Origin URI (e.g., file:///path/to/note.md,
                                  vault://my-vault/note)
  --source-type [file|url|vault|api|manual]
                                  Origin classification. Opt-in: omitted means
                                  no provenance is stamped.
  --linked-memory-ids TEXT        Comma-separated memory UUIDs to link via
                                  declared_link edges
  --linked-source-uris TEXT       Comma-separated source URIs to resolve to
                                  memories and link
  --details TEXT                  Structured details as an inline JSON object.
                                  Coordinates live under the 'location' key and
                                  must be JSON numbers, not strings:
                                  '{"location": {"lat": 35.68, "lon": 139.76}}'
  --location TEXT                 Shorthand for details.location: 'lat,lon' or
                                  'lat,lon,label'
  --observed-at TEXT              When the fact held, not the write time: YYYY-
                                  MM-DD or an ISO 8601 datetime (naive = UTC).
                                  Stored as details.observed_at (server
                                  v0.127.0+).
  --dedupe [suggest|check|off]    suggest (server default); check: write nothing
                                  when a near-duplicate exists and print it
                                  (status duplicate_candidate, exit 0: a result,
                                  not an error); off: never suggest a supersede
                                  for this memory, permanently (server
                                  v0.93.0+).
  --tags-normalize                Store each tag under the context's established
                                  spelling; lint reports each mapping as
                                  tag_normalized (server v0.93.0+).
  --help                          Show this message and exit.

  Generate an age keypair and register the public half.

  The private key is PRINTED, not stored: this SDK takes no native keychain
  dependency, so custody is yours. Save it somewhere your secret manager
  controls and point KAGURA_AGE_IDENTITY_FILE at it. Output is refused on a TTY
  unless --reveal is given.

Options:
  --profile TEXT  Your key profile  [default: default]
  --label TEXT    Human-readable label for this pubkey
  --no-register   Generate only; skip server registration
  --reveal        Allow printing the private key to a terminal
  --help          Show this message and exit.
secret pubkeys:
Usage: kagura-memory secret pubkeys [OPTIONS]

  List recipient pubkeys.

Options:
  --mine  Only your own pubkeys
  --help  Show this message and exit.
secret put:
Usage: kagura-memory secret put [OPTIONS] NAME

  Store a secret.

Options:
  --to PUBKEY_ID    Recipient pubkey id (repeatable). Default: yourself.
  --from-file PATH  Read the value from a file instead of stdin
  --profile TEXT    Your key profile  [default: default]
  --help            Show this message and exit.
secret revoke:
Usage: kagura-memory secret revoke [OPTIONS] NAME

  Revoke one recipient's grant.

Options:
  --to PUBKEY_ID  Recipient pubkey id to revoke  [required]
  --help          Show this message and exit.
secret rotate:
Usage: kagura-memory secret rotate [OPTIONS] NAME

  Rotate a secret: encrypt a NEW value to the remaining recipients.

Options:
  --from-file PATH  Read the value from a file instead of stdin
  --profile TEXT    Your key profile  [default: default]
  --help            Show this message and exit.
setup claude:
Usage: kagura-memory setup claude [OPTIONS]

  Set up Kagura Memory integration for Claude Code.

  Writes .kagura.json and a type "http" kagura-memory entry. --scope project
  puts the key in .mcp.json (0600, gitignored). --scope user runs `claude mcp
  add-json --scope user kagura-memory '<entry>'` with an entry that sends Bearer
  ${KAGURA_MCP_API_KEY}, which Claude Code reads from its environment when it
  connects: the key is on no command line and not in ~/.claude.json, and setup
  says whether this shell has the variable. A different user-scope entry is
  replaced (`claude mcp remove` runs first, and the old entry is put back if the
  add fails, unless it holds a key: then its re-add command is printed, the key
  masked); an identical one is left as it is. ~/.claude.json
  ($CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR's when set) is read, never written: an entry in a stronger
  scope (local > project > user) would hide the new one, so it stops the
  command. Local scope is the git repository's (a linked worktree's main working
  tree), and project scope the closest .mcp.json defining kagura-memory, here or
  in a parent directory, as Claude Code reads them. A re-run without
  --guardrails, --tool-profile, --add-tools or --context, or whose --mcp-url
  lacks the old entry's ?tools= allowlist, drops the earlier value, and says so.

  A context (-c, else .kagura.json's, else KAGURA_CONTEXT_ID) is matched against
  IDs and exact names on the first list_contexts page. A dashed UUID not found
  there is used as an ID; other names are searched on every page. No context
  sends no request.

  This port installs no hooks or slash commands: the Python CLI's flags for
  them, and --no-auto-context, are accepted and change nothing.

  Pass --guardrails a context id only for a context whose editor list you
  control. The server ignores any value but a UUID or off, so anything else is
  refused here.

  Examples:
    kagura-memory setup claude
    kagura-memory setup claude --profile default        # OAuth via kagura-mcp (recommended)
    kagura-memory setup claude --profile default --scope user   # one entry for every project
    kagura-memory setup claude --profile default --guardrails off --tool-profile core
    kagura-memory setup claude --profile default --add-tools explore --context CTX_UUID
    kagura-memory setup claude --api-key kagura_xxx --mcp-url http://localhost:8080/mcp/w/{workspace_id}
    kagura-memory setup claude -y --api-key kagura_xxx --context-id my-project
    kagura-memory setup claude --no-commands      # plugin users: its /kagura-memory:* instead
    kagura-memory setup claude --no-auto-context  # always show full context list

Options:
  --api-key TEXT               Kagura API key (skip prompt)
  --mcp-url URL                MCP URL
  -c, --context-id TEXT        Context ID
  --profile TEXT               OAuth profile (from `kagura auth login`) for the
                               Python CLI's kagura-mcp entry, which this port
                               cannot write: refused
  --project-dir DIR            Project directory  [default: .]
  -y, --non-interactive        Accepted for compatibility; this port never
                               prompts
  --guardrails off|CONTEXT_ID  Set the URL's guardrails parameter (server
                               v0.74.0+): a context id, or off
  --scope [project|user]       project (.mcp.json) or user (claude mcp add-
                               json); a user entry sends $KAGURA_MCP_API_KEY:
                               set it where Claude Code starts  [default:
                               project]
  --tool-profile NAME          Add ?profile=NAME to the upstream MCP URL (server
                               v0.73.0+): the tools tools/list shows. Without it
                               memory-cloud 0.93.0+ lists 'core' (21 tools on
                               0.141.0); 'full' lists every tool (72). The
                               server knows only these two (case-sensitive) and
                               fails tools/list for any other name. A profile is
                               a view, not an authorization boundary: tools/call
                               reaches an unlisted tool too. A ?tools= allowlist
                               already on the URL wins over it. An unknown name
                               leaves Claude Code with no Kagura tools.
  --add-tools NAME[,NAME...]   Add ?add_tools= to the upstream MCP URL (server
                               v0.129.0+): tools listed on top of the profile,
                               e.g. explore, which recall's explore_hints need
                               (or --tool-profile full). Comma-separated, may
                               repeat. The server ignores an unknown name, and
                               the list under a ?tools= allowlist. A re-run
                               without it drops an earlier list.
  --context CONTEXT_ID         Add ?context= to the upstream MCP URL (server
                               v0.114.0+): the default context for context-
                               scoped tools called without context_id, so a
                               session can skip list_contexts. An explicit
                               context_id wins, and the default is checked like
                               one. Unlike --context-id (the project's
                               .kagura.json), it is a UUID.
  --session-hook               Accepted for compatibility; this port installs no
                               hooks
  --no-session-hook            Accepted for compatibility; this port installs no
                               hooks
  --sync-hook                  Accepted for compatibility; this port installs no
                               hooks
  --no-sync-hook               Accepted for compatibility; this port installs no
                               hooks
  --commands                   Accepted for compatibility; this port installs no
                               commands
  --no-commands                Accepted for compatibility; this port installs no
                               commands
  --no-auto-context            Accepted for compatibility; this port never
                               prompts
  --help                       Show this message and exit.
setup codex:
Usage: kagura-memory setup codex [OPTIONS]

  Set up Kagura Memory for OpenAI Codex (CLI and IDE extension).

  Adds the kagura-memory MCP server with `codex mcp add NAME --url URL --bearer-
  token-env-var KAGURA_API_KEY`, which writes ~/.codex/config.toml
  ($CODEX_HOME); with --force the same command replaces an entry of the same
  name. Without codex on PATH, setup prints the [mcp_servers] table to add
  instead. The entry names the variable Codex reads the API key from when it
  connects (--api-key-env renames it): setup never sees the key. Check it with:
  codex mcp get kagura-memory.

  Codex reads the server's MCP instructions, so --context-id (a UUID) or
  --guardrails CONTEXT_ID puts that context's tool guardrail digest in them.
  While the kagura-memory Codex plugin's guardrail hooks are on for the entry,
  they deliver guardrails themselves, and the URL gets ?guardrails=off instead.
  A guardrails value already in the MCP URL (--mcp-url or the configured
  mcp_url) is kept. --agents-md also puts the context's export block into
  ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, fetched with the usual credential (KAGURA_API_KEY, the
  OAuth profile, .kagura.json), which must be for the entry's server.

  With --url-form --oauth (memory-cloud 0.77.0+, whose client registration
  accepts Codex; setup checks the version first), the entry is a bare URL and
  Codex then signs in itself: `codex mcp add` starts the browser sign-in, so
  setup runs it attached to this terminal (its output on stderr) only with a
  terminal on stdin and without -y, and otherwise prints the table for you to
  add and sign in with `codex mcp login NAME`. Codex keeps the token in its own
  store, keyed on the URL. The API-key URL form stays the default.

  The MCP URL must be an http(s) URL with a host. Padding, control characters
  and tabs or newlines inside it are dropped before the HTTPS check, and the
  entry gets the URL that check read.

  Pass --guardrails a context id only for a context whose editor list you
  control. The server ignores any value but a UUID or off, so anything else is
  refused here.

  Examples:
    kagura-memory setup codex --profile default
    kagura-memory setup codex --profile default --context-id CTX_UUID
    kagura-memory setup codex --url-form --mcp-url https://memory.kagura-ai.com/mcp/w/WS_ID
    kagura-memory setup codex --url-form --oauth --mcp-url https://memory.kagura-ai.com/mcp/w/WS_ID
    kagura-memory setup codex --profile default --dry-run

Options:
  --profile TEXT               OAuth profile (from `kagura auth login`) for the
                               Python CLI's kagura-mcp entry, which this port
                               cannot write: refused, and ignored with --url-
                               form
  --name TEXT                  MCP server name in the harness config: 1-64
                               letters, digits, '-' or '_', starting with a
                               letter or digit  [default: kagura-memory]
  -c, --context-id TEXT        Context ID, for the guardrails lane and the
                               AGENTS.md export only: a UUID
  --guardrails off|CONTEXT_ID  Set the URL's ?guardrails= (server v0.74.0+).
                               Codex reads the MCP instructions, which then
                               carry that context's tool guardrail digest.
                               Defaults to --context-id, or to 'off' while the
                               kagura-memory plugin's guardrail hooks are on,
                               unless the MCP URL (--mcp-url or the configured
                               mcp_url) already sets it. Use a context whose
                               editor list you control. 'off' also removes the
                               guardrails block from get_context_info. With
                               --oauth, changing it later means `codex mcp
                               login` again.
  --tool-profile NAME          Add ?profile=NAME to the upstream MCP URL (server
                               v0.73.0+): the tools tools/list shows. Without it
                               memory-cloud 0.93.0+ lists 'core' (21 tools on
                               0.141.0); 'full' lists every tool (72). The
                               server knows only these two (case-sensitive) and
                               fails tools/list for any other name. A profile is
                               a view, not an authorization boundary: tools/call
                               reaches an unlisted tool too. A ?tools= allowlist
                               already on the URL wins over it. A ?profile=
                               already in --mcp-url is kept without it.
  --add-tools NAME[,NAME...]   Add ?add_tools= to the upstream MCP URL (server
                               v0.129.0+): tools listed on top of the profile,
                               e.g. explore, which recall's explore_hints need
                               (or --tool-profile full). Comma-separated, may
                               repeat. The server ignores an unknown name, and
                               the list under a ?tools= allowlist. An
                               ?add_tools= already in --mcp-url is kept without
                               it.
  --agents-md [PATH]           Also write the context's tool guardrail export
                               block into PATH (default ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, or
                               AGENTS.override.md when it exists). Rarely
                               needed: the digest already arrives in the MCP
                               instructions. Only the marked block changes.
  --url-form                   Every entry this port writes is the URL form, so
                               this changes nothing alone; --oauth needs it. The
                               entry sends a long-lived API key from an
                               environment variable, which setup never sees;
                               with --oauth it holds no key, and the harness
                               signs in itself.
  --mcp-url URL                The MCP URL your API key works with, or that the
                               harness signs in to with --oauth
                               (…/mcp/w/<workspace>); default: the configured
                               mcp_url, else https://memory.kagura-ai.com/mcp
                               (--oauth needs it given)
  --api-key-env VAR            The variable Codex reads the API key from
                               (bearer_token_env_var; default KAGURA_API_KEY,
                               which every kagura-memory command also ranks
                               above OAuth profiles). Not with --oauth.
  --oauth                      With --url-form: a URL entry with no key. memory-
                               cloud 0.77.0+ (setup checks first) accepts
                               Codex's client registration, and Codex then signs
                               in itself: `codex mcp add` starts the browser
                               sign-in, so it runs only with a terminal and
                               without -y; otherwise setup prints the table, and
                               you sign in with `codex mcp login NAME` (--no-
                               browser when the browser cannot reach Codex's
                               loopback callback).
  --force                      Replace an existing entry of the same name
  -y, --non-interactive        Never hands the terminal to a harness CLI
                               (--oauth); nothing else here prompts
  --dry-run                    Show the command or block, the entry and the
                               AGENTS.md step; change nothing
  --api-key TEXT               Accepted for compatibility; not stored or used:
                               the entry reads the key from an environment
                               variable
  --project-dir DIR            Accepted for compatibility; not used: the entry
                               is per user, and no project file is written
  --help                       Show this message and exit.
setup hermes:
Usage: kagura-memory setup hermes [OPTIONS]

  Set up Kagura Memory for Hermes Agent.

  Prints the mcp_servers block and the config.yaml to add it to ($HERMES_HOME,
  or the active Hermes profile's: ~/.hermes/profiles/<name> when
  ~/.hermes/active_profile names one, else ~/.hermes) and, for the API-key form,
  changes nothing there: `hermes mcp add` asks for the key, and this port never
  prompts. When config.yaml already has an mcp_servers key, the entry alone is
  printed, to go under it. The entry reads the API key from MCP_<NAME>_API_KEY
  (MCP_KAGURA_MEMORY_API_KEY by default), the variable `hermes mcp add` derives
  from --name, in the .env beside config.yaml: add the key there yourself; setup
  never sees it. Check it with: hermes mcp test kagura-memory.

  Hermes does not read MCP instructions: guardrails reach it through
  get_context_info (on by default) and, if you choose, an export block
  (--agents-md with --context-id, or a --guardrails CONTEXT_ID) in the context
  file Hermes loads from this directory, so a user's own file keeps loading.
  Hermes loads only the first type it finds (.hermes.md/HERMES.md, AGENTS files,
  CLAUDE.md, Cursor rules); with only Cursor rules, name a file with --agents-md
  PATH. --guardrails off is refused, and a context id, from the flag or the URL,
  is not written; a first ?guardrails=off in the URL is kept, alone, with a
  warning.

  With --url-form --oauth (memory-cloud 0.77.0+, whose client registration
  accepts Hermes Agent; setup checks the version first), the entry is a URL with
  `auth: oauth`. With a terminal on stdin and without -y, setup runs `hermes mcp
  add NAME --url URL --auth oauth --connect-timeout 315` attached to this
  terminal (its output on stderr): Hermes signs in when it probes the server,
  within the bound `hermes mcp login` uses, which it keeps as the entry's
  connect_timeout. Setup then reads the entry back with `hermes config get` and
  stops (exit 1) when Hermes kept another entry, saved one without auth: oauth,
  or saved it disabled. With -y or without a terminal, it prints the block
  instead. Sign in later with `hermes mcp login NAME` (the browser flow), or on
  memory-cloud 0.78.0+ with `hermes mcp login NAME --flow device`, which needs
  no loopback callback. The API-key URL form stays the default.

  The MCP URL must be an http(s) URL with a host. Padding, control characters
  and tabs or newlines inside it are dropped before the HTTPS check, and the
  entry gets the URL that check read.

  Examples:
    kagura-memory setup hermes --profile default
    kagura-memory setup hermes --profile default --context-id CTX_UUID --agents-md
    kagura-memory setup hermes --url-form --mcp-url https://memory.kagura-ai.com/mcp/w/WS_ID
    kagura-memory setup hermes --url-form --oauth --mcp-url https://memory.kagura-ai.com/mcp/w/WS_ID
    kagura-memory setup hermes --profile default -y     # print the block only

Options:
  --profile TEXT               OAuth profile (from `kagura auth login`) for the
                               Python CLI's kagura-mcp entry, which this port
                               cannot write: refused, and ignored with --url-
                               form
  --name TEXT                  MCP server name in the harness config: 1-64
                               letters, digits, '-' or '_', starting with a
                               letter or digit  [default: kagura-memory]
  -c, --context-id TEXT        Context ID, for the guardrails lane and the
                               AGENTS.md export only: a UUID
  --guardrails off|CONTEXT_ID  Never written: Hermes does not read MCP
                               instructions. 'off' is refused (it would remove
                               the get_context_info guardrails block, Hermes's
                               only guardrail lane); a context UUID only picks
                               the AGENTS.md export's context. A ?guardrails=
                               context in --mcp-url is dropped too.
  --tool-profile NAME          Add ?profile=NAME to the upstream MCP URL (server
                               v0.73.0+): the tools tools/list shows. Without it
                               memory-cloud 0.93.0+ lists 'core' (21 tools on
                               0.141.0); 'full' lists every tool (72). The
                               server knows only these two (case-sensitive) and
                               fails tools/list for any other name. A profile is
                               a view, not an authorization boundary: tools/call
                               reaches an unlisted tool too. A ?tools= allowlist
                               already on the URL wins over it. A ?profile=
                               already in --mcp-url is kept without it.
  --add-tools NAME[,NAME...]   Add ?add_tools= to the upstream MCP URL (server
                               v0.129.0+): tools listed on top of the profile,
                               e.g. explore, which recall's explore_hints need
                               (or --tool-profile full). Comma-separated, may
                               repeat. The server ignores an unknown name, and
                               the list under a ?tools= allowlist. An
                               ?add_tools= already in --mcp-url is kept without
                               it.
  --agents-md [PATH]           Write the context's tool guardrail export block
                               into PATH (default: the context file Hermes loads
                               from here: the nearest .hermes.md or HERMES.md up
                               to the git root, else this directory's AGENTS
                               file, else its CLAUDE.md, else a new AGENTS.md;
                               none when only Cursor rules load, which a new
                               AGENTS.md would stop loading). Only the marked
                               block changes; an empty set removes it.
  --url-form                   Every entry this port writes is the URL form, so
                               this changes nothing alone; --oauth needs it. The
                               entry sends a long-lived API key from an
                               environment variable, which setup never sees;
                               with --oauth it holds no key, and the harness
                               signs in itself.
  --mcp-url URL                The MCP URL your API key works with, or that the
                               harness signs in to with --oauth
                               (…/mcp/w/<workspace>); default: the configured
                               mcp_url, else https://memory.kagura-ai.com/mcp
                               (--oauth needs it given)
  --api-key-env VAR            Not accepted: Hermes names the variable
                               MCP_<NAME>_API_KEY
  --oauth                      With --url-form: a URL entry with `auth: oauth`
                               and no key. memory-cloud 0.77.0+ (setup checks
                               first) accepts Hermes's client registration, and
                               Hermes then signs in itself when `hermes mcp add`
                               probes it (given --connect-timeout 315, which
                               Hermes keeps), or later with `hermes mcp login
                               NAME`; on memory-cloud 0.78.0+, `hermes mcp login
                               NAME --flow device` signs in with a code and
                               needs no loopback callback.
  --force                      Replace an existing entry of the same name
  -y, --non-interactive        Never hands the terminal to a harness CLI
                               (--oauth); nothing else here prompts
  --dry-run                    Show the command or block, the entry and the
                               AGENTS.md step; change nothing
  --api-key TEXT               Accepted for compatibility; not stored or used:
                               the entry reads the key from an environment
                               variable
  --project-dir DIR            Accepted for compatibility; not used: the entry
                               is per user, and no project file is written
  --help                       Show this message and exit.
setup openclaw:
Usage: kagura-memory setup openclaw [OPTIONS]

  Set up Kagura Memory for OpenClaw.

  Adds the kagura-memory MCP server with `openclaw mcp add NAME --url URL
  --transport streamable-http --header 'Authorization=Bearer ${KAGURA_API_KEY}'
  --no-probe`; --force replaces an entry with `openclaw mcp set`. Both write
  openclaw.json in $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR (else ~/.openclaw), or
  $OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH, which the Gateway hot-reloads. Without openclaw on
  PATH, setup prints the mcp.servers block instead. OpenClaw fills in
  ${KAGURA_API_KEY} (--api-key-env renames it) from the .env in its state
  directory: add the key there yourself; setup never sees it. Check it with:
  openclaw mcp doctor kagura-memory --probe.

  OpenClaw does not read MCP instructions: guardrails reach it through
  get_context_info (on by default) and, if you choose, an export block in
  AGENTS.md in its default workspace, $OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR or else workspace/
  in that state directory (--agents-md). As on Hermes, --guardrails off is
  refused, and a context id, from the flag or the URL, is not written; a first
  ?guardrails=off in the URL is kept, alone, with a warning.

  With --url-form --oauth (memory-cloud 0.77.0+, whose client registration
  accepts OpenClaw; setup checks the version first), the entry is a URL with
  `auth: "oauth"` and no header, which OpenClaw saves without probing: sign in
  with `openclaw mcp login NAME`, then check it with `openclaw mcp doctor NAME
  --probe`. The API-key URL form stays the default.

  The MCP URL must be an http(s) URL with a host. Padding, control characters
  and tabs or newlines inside it are dropped before the HTTPS check, and the
  entry gets the URL that check read.

  Examples:
    kagura-memory setup openclaw --profile default
    kagura-memory setup openclaw --profile default --context-id CTX_UUID --agents-md
    kagura-memory setup openclaw --url-form --mcp-url https://memory.kagura-ai.com/mcp/w/WS_ID
    kagura-memory setup openclaw --url-form --oauth --mcp-url https://memory.kagura-ai.com/mcp/w/WS_ID
    kagura-memory setup openclaw --profile default --force

Options:
  --profile TEXT               OAuth profile (from `kagura auth login`) for the
                               Python CLI's kagura-mcp entry, which this port
                               cannot write: refused, and ignored with --url-
                               form
  --name TEXT                  MCP server name in the harness config: 1-64
                               letters, digits, '-' or '_', starting with a
                               letter or digit  [default: kagura-memory]
  -c, --context-id TEXT        Context ID, for the guardrails lane and the
                               AGENTS.md export only: a UUID
  --guardrails off|CONTEXT_ID  Never written: OpenClaw does not read MCP
                               instructions. 'off' is refused (it would remove
                               the get_context_info guardrails block, OpenClaw's
                               only guardrail lane); a context UUID only picks
                               the AGENTS.md export's context. A ?guardrails=
                               context in --mcp-url is dropped too.
  --tool-profile NAME          Add ?profile=NAME to the upstream MCP URL (server
                               v0.73.0+): the tools tools/list shows. Without it
                               memory-cloud 0.93.0+ lists 'core' (21 tools on
                               0.141.0); 'full' lists every tool (72). The
                               server knows only these two (case-sensitive) and
                               fails tools/list for any other name. A profile is
                               a view, not an authorization boundary: tools/call
                               reaches an unlisted tool too. A ?tools= allowlist
                               already on the URL wins over it. A ?profile=
                               already in --mcp-url is kept without it.
  --add-tools NAME[,NAME...]   Add ?add_tools= to the upstream MCP URL (server
                               v0.129.0+): tools listed on top of the profile,
                               e.g. explore, which recall's explore_hints need
                               (or --tool-profile full). Comma-separated, may
                               repeat. The server ignores an unknown name, and
                               the list under a ?tools= allowlist. An
                               ?add_tools= already in --mcp-url is kept without
                               it.
  --agents-md [PATH]           Write the context's tool guardrail export block
                               into PATH (default AGENTS.md in the workspace
                               OpenClaw loads every session:
                               $OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR, else workspace/ in
                               $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR or ~/.openclaw). Only the
                               marked block changes.
  --url-form                   Every entry this port writes is the URL form, so
                               this changes nothing alone; --oauth needs it. The
                               entry sends a long-lived API key from an
                               environment variable, which setup never sees;
                               with --oauth it holds no key, and the harness
                               signs in itself.
  --mcp-url URL                The MCP URL your API key works with, or that the
                               harness signs in to with --oauth
                               (…/mcp/w/<workspace>); default: the configured
                               mcp_url, else https://memory.kagura-ai.com/mcp
                               (--oauth needs it given)
  --api-key-env VAR            The variable the Authorization header references,
                               kept in OpenClaw's .env ($OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR,
                               else ~/.openclaw; default KAGURA_API_KEY). Not
                               with --oauth.
  --oauth                      With --url-form: a URL entry with `auth: oauth`
                               and no key. memory-cloud 0.77.0+ (setup checks
                               first) accepts OpenClaw's client registration.
                               OpenClaw saves the entry without probing; sign in
                               with `openclaw mcp login NAME`, then run
                               `openclaw mcp doctor NAME --probe`.

Usage: kagura-memory workspace member add [OPTIONS] USER_ID

  Add an ALREADY-REGISTERED user to the workspace by user id.

  The server does not validate that USER_ID exists (v0.42.0) — a typo creates a
  dangling membership row. Prefer `kagura-memory workspace invite create
  <email>` for onboarding.

  Example:
    kagura-memory workspace member add google_1234 --role member
